title: Autologous Non-viral CRISPR/Cas Homology-directed Repair for Artemis-deficient Severe Combined Immunodeficiency
text:
There are over 500 genetic diseases that cause problems with immune deficiency or dysregulation, and a major
limitation to developing genome editing therapies at scale is the lack of methods that do not use viruses, which
are challenging and expensive to manufacture and do not work equally well for all patient’s cells. Here, I propose
to focus on one inherited immune disease, Artemis-deficient severe combined immunodeficiency (ART-SCID),
and 1) develop a pre-clinical genome editing therapy using non-viral techniques and 2) develop methods to
quickly and accurately determine if a patient has a true mutation in the gene that causes ART-SCID. If successful,
this could be translated into a clinical trial for patients with ART-SCID and have broad implications for patients
with other genetic disorders of the immune system.

title: Applying a Machine Learning and Causal Inference Approach to Analyzing Long-Term Sequelae of Viral Infection.
text:
This project aims to inform how we can repurpose medications and other interventions to reduce long-term sequelae and mortality following viral infections by analyzing electronic health record data. This work will inform infectious disease treatment strategies and advance causal inference methods for electronic health record data, strengthening our understanding of and preparedness for viral threats.

title: Mechanisms, Structures and Engineering of Flavonoid-producing Dioxygenase Enzymes
text:
The goal of this research is to enhance our understanding of the biochemistry of alpha ketoglutarate dependent
dioxygenase enzymes by studying Flavanone Synthase 1 (FLS1) and Flavanone 3-Hydroxylase (F3H), which
produce the medically significant compounds quercetin and (2S,3R)-trans-taxifolin, respectively. Methods
developed through this research will enable future studies on these and the related family of enzymes, many of
which are medically important. This research will further support public health by providing accurate enzyme
structures to serve as tools to enable the biosynthetic development of specific or novel flavonoids that can be
used to study the roles of flavonoids on the microbiome in relation to diseases associated with gut dysbiosis.

title: Project 5: Microencapsulation Delivery Vehicles for the Implementation of Precision Bioremediation at PAH-Contaminated Superfund Sites
text:
Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are contaminants of great concern commonly encountered at
Superfund sites. In this project, we will develop innovative precision bioremediation approaches that promote
PAH degradation and minimize co-contaminant mobilization. A fundamental feature of our project will be the
engineering of microcapsule delivery vehicles that facilitate targeted delivery and optimized activity of microbes
carrying out key remediation functions, ultimately reducing the potential for human and environmental exposure.

title: Shaping of offline cortical reactivations of recent experiences by pre-existing ensembles and inhibitory microcircuits
text:
Offline replay of neural activity patterns evoked by prior experiences offers a window into early stages of memory
consolidation, but the mechanisms that reshape neural representations during replay remain poorly understood.
The proposed research project will investigate the hypothesis that during spontaneous replay, neocortical activity
maps new experiences onto a pre-existing “scaffold” defined by stable recurrent connectivity. This work will
provide mechanistic insight into the nature of offline learning in the cortex and hippocampus to inform our basic
understanding of the neurobiology of memory consolidation.

title: Metabolism of dietary fatty acids promotes castration resistance in prostate cancer
text:
This proposal will investigate the molecular mechanism of which high-fatty-acid diets promote prostate
castration resistance mediated by lipid/fatty acid metabolism. We aim to determine a rate-limiting step in the
biosynthesis of fatty acyl-CoAs and myristoylated proteins that regulates androgen receptor stability and
contributes to castration resistance in prostate cancer.

title: Targeting the CDK4/6 pathway in MiT/TFE-translocation renal cell carcinoma
text:
Cancer is the second leading cause of death in the United States. Translocation renal cell carcinoma (tRCC) is
an aggressive kidney cancer without effective therapies and is an unmet medical need. This project explores
whether CDK4/6 signaling may be a defining feature of, and therapeutic vulnerability in, tRCC.

title: Novel roles of PDK4 in regulating mitochondrial protein phosphorylation, carbon flux and metabolic resilience
text:
RELEVANCE STATEMENT
Mitochondria are tiny engines that generate the chemical power that cells use to grow and function. This project
aims to understand how an enzyme known as PDK4 helps mitochondria to maintain high rates of energy
production in during normal stresses, such as food restriction and exercise. These studies will delineate the
precise role of PDK4 in regulating fuel selection and use in tissues such as muscle and heart. The results could
provide new approaches to treating metabolic disorders such as diabetes and heart disease.

title: Determining the role of a TENT5 family non-canonical polyA polymerase in Drosophila spermatogenesis
text:
In this project we will determine the role of the non-canonical polyA polymerase TENT5 in spermatogenesis in the fruit
ﬂy Drosophila melanogaster. A TENT5 gene has been linked to infer�lity in human males and our research ﬁndings will
increase our understanding about causes and treatment of human male infer�lity.

title: A cortex-midbrain circuit regulates energy balance
text:
Despite the rapidly growing rate of obesity, the development of safe and effective therapeutics has become
progressively more promising, yet is still limited, largely due to insufficient understanding of how the brain
manages energy balance. Serotonin (5-HT) remains an excellent potential target for an anti-obesity therapeutic,
but a gap in our understanding of the regulators of 5-HT persists. This proposal will focus on how 5-HT-projecting
neurons in the Agranular Insular Cortex (AIC) respond to internal and environmental cues to regulate 5-HT and
downstream metabolic mechanisms, like brown adipose tissue thermogenesis and energy balance.

title: Mentoring Translational Cancer Research in Oklahoma
text: The Oklahoma COBRE in Cancer Research supports the development of cancer research infrastructure, mentoring of early-stage investigators, and advancement of innovative cancer research programs in Oklahoma. These efforts are intended to strengthen the state’s biomedical research capacity and contribute to improved approaches for cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.

title: Novel multimodal neural, physiological, and behavioral sensing and machine learning for mental states
text:
Simultaneous brain-behavior quantification for mental states can provide novel neural-physiological markers to
enable personalized therapies for diverse mental disorders but remains immensely difficult. Our interdisciplinary
team will develop novel hardware and software tools that address several challenges on the physiology,
behavior, machine learning, and ethics fronts to enable multimodal neural-physiological-behavioral sensing and
machine learning for mental states. Our multimodal, convergent, and integrated tools will likely enable unique
brain-behavior insights into human emotion functioning applicable to broad domains of mental health.

title: Using genetics to discover mechanisms of abdominal aortic aneurysm
text:
Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) are increasingly prevalent, especially among the elderly, and can be fatal
upon rupture. Currently, there are no effective medications for AAA treatment. To address this, the study
employs a comprehensive approach involving genetics, statistics, computer analysis, biology, and mouse
models to better understand the genetics and biology of AAA, potentially leading to new treatment strategies.

title: The role of EZH1 in neuronal differentiation and neurological disorders
text:
Intellectual disabilities are group of debilitating conditions causing life-long cognitive and behavioral defects that
often remain undiagnosed and untreated. Advances in genetic studies have uncovered that defects in chromatin
regulation during cerebral cortex development significantly contribute to the pathogenic mechanisms leading to
intellectual disability. Our goal is to uncover the role of the chromatin modifier Enhancer of Zeste Homologue 1
(EZH1) in cortical neurogenesis that will ultimately provide new insights into the mechanisms and treatments for
a novel intellectual disability syndrome caused by mutations in EZH1.

title: University of New Mexico's CURE for Cancer
text: The proposed CURE for Cancer program aims to create a comprehensive research experience focused on cancer for high school and undergraduate students, and an introductory, hands-on research experience for rural middle school students. The program seeks to cultivate students' interest in science, boost their self-efficacy in science, and help them attain skills needed to apply and ultimately succeed in higher education programs and prepare them for success in graduate and professional schools. By emphasizing students from rural and under-resourced communities, the CURE for Cancer program addresses national priorities for recruiting students in STEM-Health careers, particularly in biomedical science and cancer-care workforce.

title: Enhanced Viro-Immunotherapy for Breast Cancer Brain Metastasis
text:
Breast cancer brain metastasis (BCBM) is associated with deadly outcomes due to limited therapeutic options
and poor response, urgently calling for the development of novel therapeutic intervention strategies. We have
found that oncolytic herpes simplex virus-1 (oHSV) therapy induces neutrophil infiltration and neutrophil
extracellular trap (NET) formation through induction of Insulin-like growth factor-2 (IGF2) expression and
secretion into tumor microenvironment (TME), hampering therapeutic efficacy of oHSV. In this proposed
research, we will uncover the mechanistic relationship between oHSV-induced IGF2 and oHSV-triggered
neutrophil infiltration and NET in BCBM, and characterize the preclinical therapeutic impact of novel IGF2-
scavenging oHSV in combination with radiation therapy as well as NET-mitigating oHSV for significant advance
of BCBM treatment in the future clinical application.

title: Robot-Assisted Personalized Prostate Biopsy
text:
Current systematic prostate biopsies use a one-size-fits-all biopsy plan that is still being used even in conjunction
with modern MRI-guided fusion biopsy devices, and the biopsy remains freehanded making the results variable
among urologists. We have developed novel software that optimizes the biopsy plan for each patient and a robot
that handles the ultrasound probe and automatically orients the needle-guide to follow the plan, making the
biopsy procedure hands-free and independent of physician’s skills. We have successfully completed a safety
and feasibility clinical trial, and propose a larger randomized clinical trial to investigate if our robot increases the
detection rate of clinically significant prostate cancer relative to that of a modern commercial biopsy device.

title: Novel cytoskeletal mechanisms of pathogenic bacteria interactions with intestinal epithelium
text:
Gastrointestinal disorders caused by pathogenic bacteria represent a serious health problem worldwide by
causing high mortality in infant, immunocompromised and elderly people and contributing to chronic
inflammatory conditions, such as inflammatory bowel diseases. This project will improve understanding the
pathogenesis of gastrointestinal bacterial infections by exploring novel mechanisms that regulate pathogen
interactions with intestinal epithelium and bacterial invasion into host cells. Furthermore, it will identify novel
targets for pharmacological prevention of intestinal colonization by pathogenic bacteria, which would decrease
morbidity and mortality of a large cohort of patients with enteric infections.

title: Investigating Common Molecular Pathogenic Pathways in Frontotemporal Dementia Patients iPSC-Derived Neurons
text:
Frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is the most common form of dementia before the age of 60 and about 40% of
FTD cases are familial and caused by genetic mutations in multiple genes. Common molecular pathogenic
mechanisms in FTD are largely unknown and effective treatment remains elusive. We will use patient iPSC-
derived cortical neurons with different genetic mutations as our main experimental system. A combination of
classical and cutting-edge molecular and cellular approaches (such as CRISPR editing and transcriptomic
analysis) will be employed to reveal common pathogenic mechanisms and modifier pathways in patient
neurons and identify potential therapeutic targets for FTD.

title: The contributions of quantal and nonquantal transmission to vestibular input
text:
Vestibular disfunctions can be debilitating, life-altering conditions to those affected. To develop effective
treatments, we need to understand the ways in which the vestibular system operates, and the ways in which
hair cells, the sensory organ in the vestibular system, relay information to the brain. This project seeks to
investigate a direct electrical transmission pathway between hair cells and neurons that may be playing a
larger role in synaptic transmission than previously appreciated.
